name: Powder
long_description:
Powder is an AI tool that helps wealth advisors rapidly create sales proposals that are personalized for each prospective client.  Using LLMs, Powder is able to automate a series of manual tasks such as understanding documents and conversations to create mind-blowing analysis that builds immediate trust.


Powder has 3 main features to automate sales workflows -

1. Brokerage, tax and estate document parser thats fast and accurate.
2. Meeting notetaker thats able to capture personalized insights.
3. Portfolio analysis tool that optimizes portfolio returns, risk and fees.

Our app saves hours of time and creates a pinpoint proposal that lifts a firm's ability to win new business.
one_liner: AI Agents for precise document analysis

launches.title: Playbook — AI agents that run wealth management operations
launches.tagline: AI agents that discover, execute, and verify work for wealth management firms
launches.body:
**Playbook is an AI orchestration platform for wealth management firms.**

Instead of waiting for a human to prompt an AI copilot, Playbook deploys persistent AI agents that continuously discover work, investigate it, execute workflows, and verify the results.

Today, **\~40 wealth management firms representing $660B in client assets are already on the platform.**

We’re launching Playbook publicly at:

[**https://askplaybook.ai**](https://askplaybook.ai)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110475&key=user_uploads/1254758/9eb08224-7480-445e-baba-0808170dea5f)

## The Problem

Wealth management firms have spent years digitizing their businesses.

They have CRMs, portfolio management systems, custodians, financial planning tools, document repositories, email, meeting notes, and increasingly, AI copilots.

But there’s still a fundamental problem:

**Someone has to notice that work needs to happen.**

Consider something simple.

A client normally keeps $100K in cash. One morning, that balance becomes $600K.

There may be no email.

No task.

No meeting.

No explicit instruction telling an advisor to investigate.

Someone has to notice the change, understand why it happened, determine whether action is required, gather the relevant context, decide what to do next, execute the work, and make sure it was done correctly.

AI copilots can make individual steps faster, but they still generally depend on a human to recognize the work, provide the context, and initiate the process.

That led us to a different question:

**What if the work discovered itself?**

## Introducing Playbook

Playbook is built around persistent AI agents that operate across a wealth management firm.

At the center is the **Playmaker** — an orchestration agent responsible for understanding what is happening across the firm and coordinating work.

The Playmaker delegates to specialized agents we call **Playrunners**.

Each Playrunner can be responsible for a specific domain or workflow: portfolio monitoring, tax opportunities, estate planning, client follow-up, compliance, meeting preparation, or other operational work.

Together, they operate in a continuous loop:

**Observe → Discover → Anticipate → Plan → Execute → Verify → Persist → Repeat**

Instead of asking an advisor to constantly tell AI what to do, Playbook continuously looks for work worth doing.

## How does it work?

Imagine again that a client's cash balance unexpectedly moves from $100K to $600K.

Playbook can detect the change and begin investigating.

What caused the cash increase?

Was there a security sale?

Did money arrive from an external account?

Is this expected based on an upcoming purchase or distribution?

Does the advisor already know about it?

Are there investment, tax, or planning implications?

Playbook gathers the available context, determines what it knows and what it still needs to know, and brings the advisor the information and questions required to make a decision.

From there, agents can coordinate the downstream work.

The important difference is that the advisor didn't have to discover the issue first.

**The system discovered the work.**

## Verification is the product

As we built Playbook, we became convinced that making agents capable of doing work is only half the problem.

The harder question is:

**How do you know their work is correct?**

As AI generation becomes faster and cheaper, verification becomes increasingly important — especially in financial services.

Our architecture separates execution from verification.

The agent performing a task should not simply be trusted to grade its own work.

Playbook uses independent verification steps to evaluate outputs, evidence, and completion before work is considered finished.

This creates another important principle for us:

**Appropriate autonomy, not maximum autonomy.**

Humans remain responsible for objectives, standards, risk boundaries, and judgment.

The agents handle the work within those boundaries, while consequential actions remain auditable end to end.

## Why does this matter?

The traditional question around AI in wealth management has been:

**"How many hours can we save an advisor?"**

We think there's a more interesting question.

Imagine a wealth management firm where the marginal cost of operational work approaches zero.

Suddenly, the constraint isn't just employee time.

The question becomes:

**What would you do for every client if your firm effectively had unlimited operational capacity?**

Would you review every portfolio every day?

Continuously search for tax opportunities?

Check every estate plan when circumstances change?

Prepare for every meeting automatically?

Follow up on every commitment?

Continuously verify that nothing has fallen through the cracks?

That's the future we're building toward with Playbook.

## Where we are today

Playbook is already being used by **\~40 wealth management firms representing approximately $660B in client assets.**

We're working closely with these firms to understand what happens when AI moves beyond isolated copilots and becomes an operational layer across the enterprise.

And we're just getting started.

## The Ask

We're looking for a small group of wealth management firms that want to work directly with our engineers on **enterprise-wide agentic automation**.

If you run or work at a wealth management firm, we'd love to hear about the workflows you think agents should own.

And if you're building agents yourself, we'd especially love feedback from the YC community on our approach to **persistent agents, orchestration, and independent verification.**

Check out Playbook:

[**https://askplaybook.ai**](https://askplaybook.ai)

We'd love your feedback. 👋

launches.title: Powder: Gen AI co-analyst that helps wealth advisors win new clients
launches.tagline: We automatically generate beautiful proposals that highlight an advisor's value prop
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We’re [Kanishk](https://www.linkedin.com/in/diamondk/), [Dominic](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dominic-tully-b9418292/), [SooYung](https://linkedin.com/in/soo-yung-cho-53643811), [Jeff](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeffrey-magder-3a62563/) and [David](https://www.linkedin.com/in/davidgoerz3/) from [Powder](https://powderfi.com).

\------

**TLDR**: [Powder](https://powderfi.com) is building a generative AI co-analyst to help wealth advisors win new clients by automating the sales process.

\------

**Problem**:

Wealth Advisors have an arduous sales process that has little transparency and leaves prospective clients unclear of the value they provide.

Advisors relying on their current manual operations are facing a tremendous challenge to scale.

Powder is for wealth advisors who are:

* Frustrated with burning costly analyst time making sense of prospects’ portfolio data
* Dealing with very long sales timelines to win over prospects
* Struggling to create beautiful presentations that highlight their value to prospects
* Looking to leverage the latest technology to future-proof their firm

**Solution**:

How can advisors stand out from the noise and close more prospects?

By leveraging Powder’s generative AI document and conversation extractor to rapidly leverage the prospect’s portfolio.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=77718&key=user_uploads/30926/7f9f09fd-3369-49de-b99c-7b505c81a6e2)

By fine-tuning analytics that automatically demonstrates better investment returns, reduced portfolio risk, reduced tax consequences, and lowered investment fees.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=77718&key=user_uploads/30926/14840681-c801-48df-83b2-cda90d62f686)

Creating beautiful presentations that succinctly outline the benefits to the prospective client.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=77718&key=user_uploads/30926/07d70c8a-5629-4027-bc04-879ebefca06d)

**Who are we**:

Kanishk and SooYung previously founded [RCI Navigator](https://addepar.com/addepar-navigator) (acquired by Addepar).  Navigator is being used by 150+ firms including the biggest wealth advisors on the planet such as UBS and Morgan Stanley.  We repeatedly witnessed how sales were such a massive pain point.  We carried forward our expertise on how to build for and sell to wealth advisors.

Dominic worked at Addepar as both a Senior Account Executive and Senior Account Manager. He started his career at Goldman Sachs, where he worked in the Private Wealth Management division.

David managed portfolio strategies for institutional asset owners for 33 years on mandates up to $30B in assets.

Jeff was the founding engineer at Arcade.xyz and an early BitGo employee.  He has 20 years of full-stack experience across multiple domains.

**Ask**

Interested advisors can sign up directly on our website - <https://powderfi.com> or set up a meeting with us - <https://calendly.com/powderfi/intro?month=2024-01>
